diagnostics: 30 songs failed to enroll, so every query for them scored zero. First: song-00: The submission does not expose the identify protocol.

| received MiniSearch with callables: enroll, identify | missing: identify(samples, sample_rate) | identify looks like identify but accepts only 1 positional arguments; not mapped | closest names found: identify (not mapped automatically;
only exact documented names with a plausible signature are).

| Add a submission.py at your repository root exposing enroll(song_id, samples, sample_rate) and identify(samples, sample_rate). identify returns ranked (song_id, score) pairs, best first, or [] for no match.

The score is at or below the trivial baseline (0.242), which is a whole-clip average spectrum with no peaks, no fingerprints and no time information. Beating chance (0.033) is not the bar; beating this is.
Clips from songs that were never enrolled correctly returned no match in 100% of cases.

Margin separation is not measured: there was no first-to-second margin to read on both sides (identify returned ranked ids without scores, or no out-of-database query produced one). Return (song_id, score) pairs to get this column.
252 queries raised: The submission does not expose the identify protocol.

| received MiniSearch with callables: enroll, identify | missing: identify(samples, sample_rate) | identify looks like identify but accepts only 1 positional arguments; not mapped | closest names found: identify (not mapped automatically;
only exact documented names with a plausible signature are).

| Add a submission.py at your repository root exposing enroll(song_id, samples, sample_rate) and identify(samples, sample_rate). identify returns ranked (song_id, score) pairs, best first, or [] for no match.
Weakest cell: clean_10s at 0% top-1.
Outcome split over 252 scored queries: 252 error.

metrics.help: How often the right song came back first, averaged over eight equally weighted conditions: clean, short, two noise levels, and four pitch shifts. Half of those are pitch, which the course never asks for, because it is the only condition measured to separate teams: an audited student sweep held 0.97 through the worst noise and collapsed to 10-25% at one or two semitones. Clips of songs that were never enrolled are not counted here; they are reported beside it as confident false matches. This is the leaderboard number.
metrics.label: Identification score

metrics.help: Studio-quality clips, no perturbation. The capstone's own baseline case: if this is not near 1.0, the pipeline is broken rather than merely untuned.
metrics.label: Clean top-1

metrics.help: Clips with white noise added at a target signal-to-noise ratio -- the capstone's "how well does a studio-quality clip, low-noise clip, ..., or very noisy clip match" question. Noise is added with signal_power / 10**(snr_db/10), the same formula the course uses.
metrics.label: Noisy top-1

metrics.help: The capstone's "how short of a clip can be matched" question. Fewer peaks means fewer fanout pairs, so the offset histogram has less to vote with.
metrics.label: Short clip top-1

metrics.help: Clips shifted in pitch. NOT part of the assignment -- reported because a shift moves every peak to a different frequency bin, so the (f1, f2, dt) keys stop matching. Expected behavior of the design the course teaches, shown rather than hidden.
metrics.label: Pitch-shifted top-1

metrics.help: Share of clips where the right song shared no fingerprint at all with the query. This is a fingerprinting problem: peak-picking, fanout, or a sample-rate mismatch between enroll and query.
metrics.label: No candidate found

metrics.help: Share of clips where the right song was found but something else won the tally. This is a voting problem, not a fingerprinting one -- the capstone's tally step, where votes must be counted per time offset rather than summed over every hash hit.
metrics.label: Wrong song ranked first

metrics.help: 1/N for a catalog of N songs: what naming a song at random scores. The floor every other number on this page should be read against.
metrics.label: Chance

metrics.help: Whole-clip mean log spectrum, nearest neighbour. No peaks, no fingerprints, no offsets -- none of the capstone. Beating chance is not evidence of a working pipeline; beating this is the first sign that the fingerprinting is doing something.
metrics.label: Trivial baseline

metrics.help: Median wall-clock time for one identify call, after warm-up. Reported, never scored.
metrics.label: Median identify time
